$comment: Post-quantum migration facts for cryptographic assets (cdxgen/cdxgen#4592). Each class cites the table or section its dates and members come from: NIST IR 8547 (final, October 2026), https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/8547/final, and, for DSA, FIPS 186-5. lib/inventory/pqcMigration.js classifies an asset by algorithmFamily, then OID, then normalised name (lower case, letters and digits only), and turns the class into a risks.risks[] entry. The likelihood and impact levels are cdxgen's fixed rating per class, not values from the IR; docs/CDX_CONVERT.md (CycloneDX 2.0, post-quantum migration risks) documents them, and docs/CUSTOM_PROPERTIES.md the cdx:crypto:pqc:* properties.
$excludedNote: Not classified, because IR 8547 Tables 2 and 4 do not list them: RSAES-PKCS1 (SP 800-56B specifies RSA key transport with OAEP and KTS, not PKCS #1 v1.5 encryption) and X3DH (a Signal protocol, not an SP 800-56A scheme). Quantum-safe per IR 8547 Tables 3 and 5-8, so no risk: ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, LMS/HSS, XMSS, ML-KEM, AES, Ascon, and SHA-2/SHA-3 members with at least 128 bits of collision strength.
$unclassifiedPrimitivesNote: NIST IR 8547 Section 3.2.1: a hybrid (composite) key-establishment scheme combines the shared secrets of its component schemes and is approved when one input comes from an approved scheme, so a combiner is not classified by the OID of one of its inputs.

minimumKeySizes.$comment: Smallest key size per key family with the 112 bits of classical security strength that IR 8547 Table 2 (ECDSA, RSA) and Table 4 (finite-field and elliptic-curve DH and MQV, RSA) list as the approved parameters. Key sizes for 112 bits: SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 Table 2 (RSA k = 2048, FFC L = 2048, ECC f = 224).

namedGroupKeySizes.$comment: Finite-field groups whose name carries no separate key size: the ffdhe groups of RFC 7919, whose modulus size is the number in the name.

quantum-vulnerable-signature.source: NIST IR 8547 Table 2 (quantum-vulnerable digital signature algorithms): ECDSA and RSA at >= 112 bits, EdDSA at >= 128 bits of classical security strength [FIPS186]
quantum-vulnerable-signature.statement: This digital signature algorithm is quantum-vulnerable; NIST IR 8547 Table 2 deprecates it after 2030 and disallows it after 2035.
quantum-vulnerable-signature.rationale: {algorithm} is a quantum-vulnerable digital signature algorithm listed in NIST IR 8547 Table 2: deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035.

quantum-vulnerable-key-establishment.source: NIST IR 8547 Table 4 (quantum-vulnerable key-establishment schemes): finite-field DH and MQV, elliptic-curve DH and MQV [SP80056A] and RSA [SP80056B], at >= 112 bits of classical security strength
quantum-vulnerable-key-establishment.statement: This key-establishment scheme is quantum-vulnerable; NIST IR 8547 Table 4 deprecates it after 2030 and disallows it after 2035.
quantum-vulnerable-key-establishment.rationale: {algorithm} is a quantum-vulnerable key-establishment scheme listed in NIST IR 8547 Table 4: deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035.

quantum-vulnerable-public-key.source: NIST IR 8547 Table 2 (ECDSA, RSA [FIPS186]) and Table 4 (elliptic-curve DH and MQV [SP80056A], RSA [SP80056B]): the key algorithm alone does not say which use applies, and both tables give the same transition
quantum-vulnerable-public-key.statement: This public-key algorithm is quantum-vulnerable whether it signs (NIST IR 8547 Table 2) or establishes keys (Table 4); both tables deprecate it after 2030 and disallow it after 2035.
quantum-vulnerable-public-key.rationale: {algorithm} is a quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithm listed in NIST IR 8547 Table 2 and Table 4: deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035.

below-minimum-strength.source: NIST IR 8547 Table 2 and Table 4 list only parameters with >= 112 bits of classical security strength; key sizes per SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 Table 2
below-minimum-strength.transition: Below the minimum strength of the currently approved parameters in NIST IR 8547 Table 2 and Table 4
below-minimum-strength.statement: This key is below the 112 bits of classical security strength that NIST IR 8547 Tables 2 and 4 list for the currently approved quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms.
below-minimum-strength.rationale: {algorithm} uses a {size}-bit key, below the {minimum}-bit minimum (112 bits of classical security strength) of the parameters NIST IR 8547 Table 2 and Table 4 list.

hash-sha1.source: NIST IR 8547 Table 8 (hash functions and XOFs), footnote 4
hash-sha1.transition: Currently deprecated for all remaining technical applications; disallowed for use in FIPS-validated cryptographic modules after 2030
hash-sha1.statement: SHA-1 is currently deprecated for all remaining technical applications and will be disallowed for use in FIPS-validated cryptographic modules after 2030 (NIST IR 8547 Table 8, footnote 4).
hash-sha1.rationale: {algorithm} is SHA-1, whose collision security strength is below 80 bits (NIST IR 8547 Table 8); it is currently deprecated and disallowed in FIPS-validated modules after 2030.

symmetric-112-bit.source: NIST IR 8547 Section 4.1.3 and Table 8: SHA-224, SHA-512/224 and SHA3-224 have 112 bits of collision security strength
symmetric-112-bit.statement: This algorithm provides 112 bits of security; NIST IR 8547 section 4.1.3 says NIST's symmetric standards at the 112-bit security level will be disallowed in 2030.
symmetric-112-bit.rationale: {algorithm} has 112 bits of collision security strength (NIST IR 8547 Table 8); section 4.1.3 says the 112-bit symmetric standards will be disallowed in 2030.

dsa-generation-not-approved.source: FIPS 186-5 (February 2023), section 4 (The Digital Signature Algorithm) and Appendix E: DSA is no longer approved for digital signature generation and may be used to verify signatures generated prior to the implementation date of FIPS 186-5; NIST IR 8547 Table 2 does not list it
dsa-generation-not-approved.transition: No longer approved for digital signature generation; may be used only to verify signatures generated prior to the implementation date of FIPS 186-5
dsa-generation-not-approved.statement: FIPS 186-5 no longer approves DSA for digital signature generation; DSA may be used only to verify signatures generated prior to the implementation date of FIPS 186-5 (section 4).
dsa-generation-not-approved.rationale: {algorithm} is DSA, which FIPS 186-5 (section 4) no longer approves for digital signature generation; it may be used only to verify signatures generated prior to the implementation date of FIPS 186-5.
